results.question: Read a few Loki log excerpts matching {job=~".+"} in this window. Report whether actual timestamped log lines were returned.

result.subject: Observability benchmark
result.summary: Yes, actual timestamped log lines were returned from Loki. The query {job=~".+"} over the window produced 10 log excerpts (the requested limit), each with a nanosecond-precision Loki timestamp and a structured JSON line containing its own application-level timestamp, service name, HTTP method/path, status, duration, and trace ID. Services observed include api-gateway, payment-service, order-service, and webapp. The read was marked incomplete because the source held more entries than the 10-entry limit, confirming there is substantial log volume in the window.

impact.summary: No incident impact — this was a read verification question.

findings.statement: Loki returned actual timestamped log lines for the query {job=~".+"} in the window 2026-10-28T04:58:52Z to 2026-10-29T04:58:52Z. 10 excerpts were retrieved (limit=10), with Loki timestamps spanning 2026-10-29T04:53:41Z to 2026-10-29T04:57:46Z, across services api-gateway, payment-service, order-service, and webapp. Each entry carries a JSON line with its own application-level timestamp, service name, HTTP method/path, status code, duration, and trace_id. The result was marked incomplete because more entries exist beyond the 10-entry limit, confirming substantial log volume in the window.
findings.mechanism: Loki query {job=~".+"} returned structured log entries with nanosecond-precision timestamps and JSON-formatted log lines within the requested window
